desc:
citations[i] is the number of citations received by the i-th paper of a researcher. The researcher's h-index is the largest integer h such that at least h papers have h or more citations each.

Return the h-index. An h-index of 0 is always possible.

For example, [3, 0, 6, 1, 5] gives 3: three papers have at least 3 citations, but there are not four papers with at least 4.
hints: Sorting the array in descending order and finding the last position i with citations[i] ≥ i + 1 works in O(n log n).
The answer can never exceed n, the number of papers, so every citation count above n can be treated as exactly n.

Make an array bucket[0..n] where bucket[c] counts papers with min(c, n) citations. Walk h from n down to 0, accumulating the number of papers with at least h citations, and stop at the first h where that total is at least h.
editorial: Let n be the number of papers. Since h cannot exceed n, clamp every citation count to n and count them into bucket[0..n]. Now iterate h from n down to 0 while keeping papers, the number of papers with at least h citations (add bucket[h] at each step). The first h with papers ≥ h is the largest valid one.

This is a counting sort on a clamped range, so it runs in O(n) time and O(n) space, compared to O(n log n) for sorting. Correctness comes from monotonicity: as h decreases, papers only grows, while h shrinks, so the first success scanning downward is the maximum.
